provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The original mechanism splits the input into square panels at full separator columns of colour 6. It then drops each panel's piece, in left-to-right order, into an empty background canvas. Each piece keeps its cross-gravity coordinates, enters with its leading face at the canvas edge opposite gravity, and falls rigidly until the next step would leave the canvas or hit a filled cell. The factory pushes two direction vectors through the D4 transform: gravity, originally (1,0), and panel order, originally (0,1). A row reversal negates the column component; each clockwise rotation maps (dr,dc) to (dc,-dr). The emitted program works directly in visible coordinates. If the order vector is horizontal, it splits panels at full SEP columns; otherwise it splits at full SEP rows. It sorts panels along the transformed order direction. For each piece, it shifts the piece along gravity so its smallest projection onto gravity sits on the canvas entry edge, then steps it along gravity while every cell stays in bounds and lands on background. Because every panel is square, the global transform acts on each panel exactly as it acts on the output canvas, so panel-local coordinates map one-to-one onto canvas coordinates. Background and separator are the constants palette[7] and palette[6]; piece colours are copied unchanged.
draft_notes.limitations: Assumes separators are complete lines of palette[6] and that the background is exactly palette[7], as the constructor guarantees. Panels are assumed equal-sized, and the canvas size is taken from the first panel. Pieces that would collide on entry are still stamped by the same fall rule, matching the reference simulation; the generator never produces such scenes. The demonstrations are not used, since all roles are fixed by d4 and palette. The fixtures are consistent with the uniform rule, and no contradictions were found.
